spec: Given a 2D grid of integers, determine whether its values form a checkerboard pattern, meaning every cell differs from each of its horizontally and vertically adjacent neighbours, with exactly two distinct values used alternately based on whether the sum of a cell's row and column index is even or odd. A grid with a single cell, or an empty grid, counts as a valid checkerboard.

Given a 2D grid of integers and a non-negative integer k, return a new grid in which the rows have been cyclically shifted downward by k positions, so that a row that would shift past the bottom reappears at the top. The shift amount k may be larger than the number of rows, in which case it should wrap around (use k modulo the number of rows). An empty grid always returns an empty grid.

Parse a string of semicolon-separated key=value pairs like "a=1;b=2;c=3" into a dict mapping key to value (both as strings, unmodified). If the same key appears more than once, the later occurrence overwrites earlier ones. An empty string input returns an empty dict. Keys and values are taken exactly as they appear (no stripping), and values never contain a ";" character.

Split a single simple CSV row into a list of field strings. Fields are separated by commas; there is no quoting mechanism and fields never contain commas or quote characters. Do not trim whitespace from fields. An empty string input represents a single empty field and must return a list containing one empty string.

Compare two semantic version strings of the form "MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH" (all non-negative integers, no pre-release or build suffixes). Return -1 if the first version is older than the second, 1 if it is newer, and 0 if they are equal. Comparison must be done numerically component by component, not lexicographically (so "1.10.0" is newer than "1.9.0").

Given a version string "MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH" and a part name that is one of "major", "minor", or "patch", return the new version string after incrementing that part by 1. Incrementing "major" resets minor and patch to 0. Incrementing "minor" resets patch to 0 and leaves major unchanged. Incrementing "patch" leaves major and minor unchanged.

Parse a string of the form "Name <email>" where Name is arbitrary text (which may include spaces) followed by a space, then an email address enclosed in angle brackets. Return a tuple (name, email) with the name's surrounding whitespace stripped and the email exactly as it appeared inside the brackets. Assume the input always contains exactly one "<" and one ">" and the format is well-formed.
Parse a dimension string of the form "WIDTHxHEIGHT" (positive integers separated by a lowercase "x") into a tuple (width, height) of ints.

Parse a duration string composed of an optional hours part "Nh" followed by an optional minutes part "Nm" (e.g. "1h30m", "2h", "45m"), where N is a non-negative integer, and return the total number of minutes as an int. At least one of the two parts is always present, and when both are present the hours part always comes first with no separator between them.

Parse a geographic coordinate string of the form "lat,lon" where lat and lon are decimal numbers (each may include a leading "-" and a decimal point) into a tuple of two floats (lat, lon). There is no space around the comma.

Parse an RGB hex color string of the form "#RRGGBB" (a "#" followed by exactly six uppercase or lowercase hexadecimal digits) and return a tuple (r, g, b) of integers in 0-255, one per two-digit component.
Parse a date string in the form "YYYY-MM-DD" (4-digit year, 2-digit month, 2-digit day) and return a tuple (year, month, day) of integers.
Parse an IPv4 address string of the form "A.B.C.D" (four decimal octets separated by dots, each in 0-255) into a tuple of four ints (A, B, C, D).

Parse a single line of an INI-style config in the form "key = value" (whitespace optionally surrounding the "=" sign; the key never contains "=" or whitespace) into a tuple (key, value) with both strings stripped of leading/trailing whitespace. The value itself may contain internal whitespace, and may be empty.

Parse an HTTP-style header line of the form "Key: Value" (a colon followed by a single space, then the value) into a tuple (key, value) with the key converted to lowercase and the value stripped of surrounding whitespace. Assume the value itself never contains a colon-space sequence.

Convert a string representing a boolean value into an actual Python bool. The strings "true", "yes", and "1" (in any mix of uppercase/lowercase letters) map to True; the strings "false", "no", and "0" (in any mix of uppercase/lowercase letters) map to False. Assume the input is always one of these six strings, in any casing.

Parse a simple arithmetic expression string containing exactly two non-negative integers separated by a single operator character, one of "+", "-", "*", "/" (no spaces), and return the numeric result. For "+", "-", and "*" return an int; for "/" perform true division and return a float.

Parse a string representing an integer formatted with commas as thousands separators (e.g. "1,234,567") and return the integer value. The string never has a leading "+" but may have a leading "-" for negative numbers, and commas only ever appear correctly positioned as thousands separators.

Parse a simple URL string of the form "scheme://host/path?query" where the "/path" and "?query" portions are each optional, and return a dict with keys "scheme", "host", "path", and "query". "scheme" is everything before "://"; "host" is everything after "://" up to (but not including) the next "/" or "?" or the end of the string; "path" is everything from the "/" (inclusive) up to (but not including) "?" if present, or an empty string if there is no path; "query" is everything after "?" if present, or an empty string otherwise.

Split a Unix-style file path string into its non-empty path segments as a list of strings. The path uses "/" as separator; ignore any leading slash, trailing slash, and collapse any run of consecutive slashes (empty segments are dropped entirely). The root path "/" (or an empty string) returns an empty list.

Parse a sports score string of the form "A-B" (two non-negative integers separated by a hyphen, representing the home team score and the away team score) into a tuple (home_score, away_score) of ints.

Given a comma-separated string of tags (each tag possibly surrounded by whitespace), return the number of distinct tags after stripping whitespace from each. Comparison of tags for uniqueness is case-sensitive.

Parse a version string that consists of three dot-separated non-negative integers, optionally prefixed with a lowercase "v" (e.g. "v1.2.3" or "1.2.3"), and return a tuple (major, minor, patch) of ints.

Parse a multi-line string where each line has the form "key: value" (a colon followed by a single space, then the rest of the line as the value), with lines separated by newline characters "\n", into a dict mapping keys to values. If a key repeats on a later line, the later value overwrites the earlier one. An empty input string returns an empty dict.

Parse a single line from a ".env"-style file of the form "KEY=VALUE", where VALUE may optionally be enclosed in a matching pair of single quotes or double quotes. Return a tuple (key, value); if VALUE was quoted (its first and last characters are the same quote character and it is at least two characters long), the returned value has those surrounding quote characters removed and the inner content used as-is; otherwise the value is used exactly as it appears. The key never contains "=", quotes, or whitespace.

Given a non-negative integer number of minutes, format it as a duration string "XhYm" showing hours and remaining minutes, e.g. 90 becomes "1h30m". Omit the hours part entirely if there are zero whole hours, and omit the minutes part entirely if the remainder is zero minutes, except that a total of exactly 0 minutes must be formatted as "0m".

Parse a comma-separated specification of integers and integer ranges, such as "1,3,5-7,10", where each comma-separated token is either a single non-negative integer or a range "A-B" with A <= B, and return the sorted list of unique integers that the specification covers.

events is a list of (op, amount) tuples where op is "deposit" or "withdraw" and amount is a non-negative number. Starting from a balance of 0, apply each event in order: a deposit adds amount to the balance; a withdrawal subtracts amount from the balance only if doing so would not take the balance below -overdraft_limit, otherwise the withdrawal is skipped entirely and the balance is unchanged. Return the final balance after processing all events.

events is a list of (item, delta) tuples where item is a string and delta is an int (positive to add stock, negative to remove stock). Maintain a running count per item, starting at 0 the first time that item is mentioned. Apply each delta only if the resulting count would stay greater than or equal to 0; otherwise skip that event, leaving the item's count unchanged. Return a dict mapping every item that appeared in at least one event to its final count.

An elevator starts at floor start_floor and can only travel between min_floor and max_floor inclusive. commands is a list of strings: "UP" moves the elevator up one floor unless it is already at max_floor (in which case it stays), "DOWN" moves it down one floor unless it is already at min_floor (in which case it stays), and any other string (e.g. "OPEN", "CLOSE") has no effect on the floor. Return the final floor after processing all commands in order.

A traffic light cycles forever through RED, then GREEN, then YELLOW, then back to RED, where durations is a tuple (red_ticks, green_ticks, yellow_ticks) giving how many ticks each phase lasts. At tick 0 the light has just turned RED. Given n_ticks (a non-negative integer), return the light's state, as one of the strings "RED", "GREEN", or "YELLOW", at that tick.

Simulate a FIFO queue. commands is a list where each item is either ("enqueue", value) which adds value to the back of the queue, or ("dequeue",) which removes the item at the front of the queue if the queue is non-empty (doing nothing if the queue is already empty). Return the final contents of the queue as a list, ordered from front to back.
